issues.title: Nonhomogeneous coercivity bound
issues.failure_explanation: The statement asserts a degree-one lower bound for a quadratic form on a vector space. Scaling v to tv contradicts it for sufficiently small nonzero t. The proposition's proof instead derives the homogeneous estimate with the squared H1 norm.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition Prop2 is false as written, but its proof and the later uses already employ the intended squared coercivity estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side in Proposition Prop2 by C times the squared H1 norm of v. No proof or downstream argument needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The left-hand side is a quadratic form, scaling rules out the displayed degree-one bound, and the old appendix proof already derives the squared-norm estimate. The missing exponent has one uniquely forced correction and no inference relies on the literal expression.

issues.title: Nonlinear source estimated in an unavailable L2 space
issues.failure_explanation: From f-continu, the source is bounded by |phi|(|phi|^theta+|psi|^theta)|phi-psi|. With only H1 embedded in L6 in dimension three, the assumptions theta<3 place this product naturally in L^{6/5} when phi-psi is measured in L^{p0}, but they do not place it in L2 throughout the allowed range. Thus the old proof of the local continuity properties uses an unavailable source norm.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof of Property-P's nonlinear continuity estimates is incomplete, leaving each later convergence argument that invokes those estimates unsupported until the source-space estimate is repaired.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the proof of Property-P, estimate the nonlinear source in L^{6/5}, hence in H^{-1}, rather than in L2. Coercivity gives the required H1 bound after applying the inverse preconditioner, and Hölder's inequality with p0=6/(4−theta) bounds |phi|(|phi|^theta+|psi|^theta)|phi−psi| in L^{6/5}. Apply the same dual-space treatment to the analogous nonlinear source estimates; Property-P and every listed dependent result then retain their stated conclusions and rates.
issues.why_classification: The L2 step is a genuine invalid inference, so this is not a typo. Nevertheless, replacing it by the standard L^{6/5}–H^{-1} estimate is a short, routine Sobolev-duality correction already supported by the stated exponents and assumptions. It preserves all continuity estimates and the entire affected convergence chain without weakening any guarantee.

issues.title: Invalid weak-continuity step in global convergence
issues.failure_explanation: The old proof has only a weakly convergent H1 subsequence when it invokes Property-P(iii). That proposition controls differences under strong H1 or Lp convergence and therefore does not justify the asserted weak convergence of the nonlinear Riemannian gradients or multiplier convergence. Without a separate compactness passage, stationarity and the claimed strong H1 subsequence convergence do not follow.
issues.overall_effect: Part (ii) of Global-Convergence lacks a valid proof of stationarity and strong H1 subsequence convergence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: From the bounded H1 sequence, extract a subsequence converging weakly in H1 and strongly in every Lp with p<6 by Rellich–Kondrachov; strong L2 convergence also places the limit in the constraint manifold. Combine this Lp convergence, the established compact-difference estimates such as L-H1 and L-I, the vanishing gradient residual, and the multiplier/energy identity to pass to the stationary equation. The resulting convergence of the quadratic energy norm then upgrades the subsequence to strong H1 convergence and yields the stated multiplier convergence.
issues.why_classification: The asserted weak continuity is invalid, but a standard, local compactness-and-bootstrap passage using estimates already proved in the old source establishes every conclusion of Global-Convergence(ii). No new lemma, altered hypothesis, or weakened stationarity or convergence guarantee is required.

issues.title: Invalid summability estimate in the local-convergence induction
issues.failure_explanation: The retraction expansion gives phi^{j+1}-phi^j=tau d_j+o(||d_j||), so its H1 norm is controlled by one power of ||d_j||, not two. Consequently, geometric decay of ||d_j|| squared must first be square-rooted before controlling cumulative displacement. The old quadratic path-length estimate leaves the neighborhood induction unclosed.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not show that all iterates remain in the neighborhood where the PL and dissipation estimates apply, so the local rate and its downstream sharper rate and error equivalence are not established by that proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the retraction expansion to bound each displacement by C times the norm of d_j, not its square. If the established estimate is ||d_j||^2 ≤ C q^j(E(phi^0)−E_S), sum the resulting bound ||d_j|| ≤ C q^{j/2}sqrt(E(phi^0)−E_S). Together with the local quadratic bound on the initial energy gap, choosing the initial neighborhood sufficiently small closes the induction. The local rate and both listed dependent results then remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The proof genuinely uses the wrong power, but taking the square root of the existing geometric estimate and summing the resulting geometric series is a short, routine local correction. It requires only adjusted neighborhood constants and preserves the method, hypotheses, conclusions, and rates throughout the affected chain.

issues.title: Local dissipation applies the spectral upper bound outside its domain

failure_location.quote: Using {\bf Proposition \ref{Property-P}}-$(i)$, the following upper bound estimate holds

issues.failure_explanation: The old proof needs to bound the Hessian quadratic form on a projected descent direction known only to be tangent. Its cited upper Rayleigh bound applies only on the smaller symmetry-normal space N_{phi_g}M. Since membership in that smaller space is not established, the local dissipation estimate does not follow with the old L.
issues.overall_effect: The stated local step-size range and contraction factors are not established with the old definition of L, affecting the local convergence theorem, the sharper preconditioned rate, and the error-equivalence corollary.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the lower constant mu as the infimum of the generalized Rayleigh quotient over the symmetry-normal space, but define the upper constant L as its supremum over the full tangent space. Use this tangent-space upper bound in the local dissipation lemma and propagate the corrected L through the admissible step-size interval, contraction factors, Local-Convergence, Var-P-convergence, E-eq-Phi, and the associated numerical rate descriptions.
issues.why_classification: This is a contained repair that avoids new proof architecture and leaves a recognizably comparable local-convergence chain. It exceeds a minor repair because enlarging the domain defining L can increase L and thereby weaken the advertised step-size and convergence-rate guarantees; the old normal-space constant does not control the merely tangent descent direction.

issues.title: Fixed regularization does not establish superlinear convergence

failure_location.quote: Furthermore,  reducing $\sigma_0$ appropriately, one can achieve a P-RG with superlinear local  convergence rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that reducing the fixed positive regularization parameter yields superlinear local convergence. The old paper actually establishes, for each fixed admissible sigma_0, a linear geometric bound with mu<1 and L=1; it gives no varying-sigma_0 algorithm or analysis proving that successive-error ratios tend to zero. The material mismatch is therefore linear versus superlinear convergence order.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed superlinear guarantee must be withdrawn; the formal local linear convergence theorem remains the supported result.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the superlinear-convergence assertion and replace it with the supported statement that, for each fixed admissible positive sigma_0, the theorem gives linear geometric convergence and that reducing sigma_0 can improve its linear contraction factor. State that superlinear convergence would require a varying-regularization or unregularized algorithm together with a new convergence analysis and is not established here.
issues.why_classification: No supported contained repair preserves a comparable superlinear guarantee: the old analysis proves only linear convergence for every fixed sigma_0. Replacing superlinear convergence by an improved linear rate removes the claim's central convergence-order guarantee and is therefore major mathematical loss, while proving the original claim would require essentially new algorithmic and proof architecture.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: appropriately reducing $\sigma_0$ improves the linear convergence rate. However, it remains an open question whether superlinear or even quadratic convergence can be achieved
